subject: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Sullivan <andrew.sullivan@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff

Hi Andrew — great to meet yesterday. Per our discussion I’m sending the proposed commercial path for the observability add-ons you asked about: retention (hot + cold tiers), distributed tracing (ingest & storage), and Advanced Dashboards (seat + manifest). I attached a compact ratecard and a workbook with two pricing scenarios (metered vs slab).

Key ask from you: confirm the three priorities (1) keep 90-day hot retention, (2) want tracing ingest metered separately, (3) Advanced Dashboards for up to 25 users initially.

What we can offer up-front: a pilot concession of 25% credit applied to addon charges for the first 90 days, plus one-time migration credit to cover initial re-ingest. If you can commit to a 12-month annual commit for base inference usage we can layer an additional 10% discount on addon line items (applies after pilot).

Next steps: please confirm priorities and whether Skyline prefers metered tracing or a fixed slab. If you accept we’ll route to Kimberly in commercial to draft the SOW and route to legal. I’ve copied a link to the workbook and attached the PDF ratecard.

Attachments: ops_addons_ratecard_20250630.pdf, skyline_price_workbook_v3.xlsx

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Andrew Sullivan <andrew.sullivan@skylinehealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@zenwell.io>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff

Jordan — thanks for the summary and the workbook. Quick answers: priorities confirmed. We strongly prefer metered tracing ingest (we need per-ingest visibility for internal cost allocation). For retention, Skyline needs the ability to spike hot retention to 120 days during clinical audit windows — is that possible under the pilot?

On pricing: the 25% pilot credit is helpful, but given the volume and that this will support our three production services, our procurement team is asking if Redwood can do 35% for the first 12 months (not only pilot). Our CFO is sensitive to add-on line items in year 1.

If you can get closer to 30–35% overall discount for year 1, we can move quickly on a 12‑month commit for the base inference. Otherwise we’ll need to evaluate the slab option and consider a shorter pilot window.

Also please call out any retention egress or re-ingest fees in the SOW — our security team will review.

—Andrew Sullivan
Director of Platform Engineering
Skyline Health
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Andrew Sullivan <andrew.sullivan@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff

Andrew — looping in Kimberly (commercial pricing) and Ben (solutions). Appreciate the clarity. We can do the metered tracing path you prefer; we’ll expose per-project ingest metrics and a tagging pattern so Skyline can attribute costs.

Counter-proposal from Redwood commercial: we can increase the first-year concession to 30% on addon charges if Skyline signs a 12-month base commit for inference (minimum ARR threshold spelled out in the attached workbook). The 30% would be structured as: 25% up-front pilot credit applied to month 1–3 addon invoices, plus a 5% true-up credit across months 4–12 contingent on commit attainment.

On the 120-day hot retention spike: we can support scheduled spikes (audit windows) but they are treated as temporary hot-tier egress/compute events; we’ll include a spike-surcharge cap in the SOW to avoid runaway costs. Ben — can you confirm the technical implementation and approximate surcharge?

Next operational steps: Kimberly to prepare a commercial term sheet + SOW redline. I’ll put a DocuSign link once legal okays the language. If that sounds doable we can schedule a short call Thursday to finalize.

Attachments: skyline_price_workbook_v3.xlsx (version with commit thresholds)

Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Andrew Sullivan <andrew.sullivan@skylinehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jul 2025 10:11:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff

Andrew / team — quick note from commercial and finance perspective. We can approve the 30% first-year concession as Jordan outlined but with the following guardrails: (1) the 12-month commit must reach the minimum ARR threshold in the workbook; (2) the 25% pilot credit applies only to addon invoice line items and cannot be applied retroactively; (3) spike-surcharge cap for retention windows will be defined as a percentage of monthly addon spend (suggest 40% cap for audit windows).

Legal will require the spike cap and a clause that documents expected tagging/metrics for metering. We recommend the following plug-in language for the SOW: "Pilot Credit applied to addon charges for first 90 days; commit true-up applied month 4–12 upon verified commit attainment; audit spike surcharge capped at 40% of monthly addon spend unless mutually agreed."

If Skyline can accept those constraints, we’ll prepare a redline SOW and a short amendment to the master services agreement. I’ve started a pricing sheet and will attach a single-sheet summary to the DocuSign envelope.

Kimberly Park
Commercial Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Andrew Sullivan <andrew.sullivan@skylinehealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jul 2025 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Observability add-ons commercial alignment & billing handoff

Kimberly — that structure is acceptable. Skyline will sign the 12‑month commit at the ARR threshold in the workbook in exchange for the 30% first-year concession (25% pilot + 5% true-up). We accept the 40% spike cap for audit windows.

Please send the SOW redline and the DocuSign link. We’ll have our procurement/legal run a quick review once it hits DocuSign and aim to return signed within 5 business days. Also please call out the operational runbook for scheduled retention spikes so our on-call and security teams know the process.

Final ask from our side: can Redwood add a one-time migration credit to offset re-ingest costs? If so, include the credit as an explicit line item in the SOW.

Thanks — we’re ready to proceed once we have the SOW.

—Andrew Sullivan
Director of Platform Engineering
Skyline Health
